label: r3c2
name: mirror head, lr 0.002
hypothesis: Same as r1c2 but with the learning rate doubled to 0.002, still decaying linearly to 0. Training success was still rising at the end, so learning seems limited by how fast the policy improves per update, and a larger step should get further on the same 158k samples. Refuted if the 2-seed mean is at or below 0.87, or if a seed becomes unstable or collapses to DONE. That would mean step size is not the bottleneck.
last_analysis: Mirroring the trunk features to match the hidden landing rule is what makes learning work. Without it the agent collapses to DONE. With the default recipe it reaches 0.53, and with more, smaller updates (128 envs, 3 epochs) about 0.88–0.89. Doubling lr to 0.002 gave the best result so far, 0.93, with both seeds at 0.93. The other changes landed within noise of 0.89: longer horizon (0.876), 2 epochs (0.886) and a four-view flip bank (0.90). A 3x3 head projection did worse (0.65) because it is costly and gets fewer samples. Learned remapping (r1c3) and very small batches (r2c1) failed. Dev IoU is about 0.99, so the remaining failures are mostly overhang and ordering errors. One trace has matching column heights but the wrong cells filled. This is the last round, so I will refine the r3c2 recipe, which has the best evidence behind it, with one change per candidate: a higher lr, more samples, or less entropy for sharper greedy policies.
